links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of LLM-based Chain-of-Verification for detecting problematic citations versus expert adjudication
links.effect: CoVe detected 60 of 62 problematic references (sensitivity 96.8%, specificity 98.6%), including every misattribution and fabrication.
links.quote: Against an expert-adjudicated set of 270 references, an LLM-based Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) detected 60 of 62 problematic references (sensitivity 96.8%, specificity 98.6%), including every misattribution and fabrication.

links.outcome: Proportion of problematic references in LLM-generated medical manuscripts verified against PubMed
links.effect: Problematic references were 11.5% of GPT-5.5 output, 29.2% of Claude output, and 29.6% of Gemini output (P < 0.001); misattribution made up 77% of errors, fabrication 0.6%.
links.quote: Problematic references accounted for 11.5% of GPT-5.5 output, 29.2% of Claude output, and 29.6% of Gemini output (P < 0.001), with no significant gradient across topics of differing publication volume (P = 0.052).
